decisions.reason: The shared terminal treatment gains an objective overlay criterion requiring the É accent and approved Hero V terminal to match exactly.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi Abdulbari,

This is much closer. I think the family is finally beginning to feel like one architectural language, and I really like the relationship between the hero V, lowercase v, and É.

I do have two remaining thoughts.

First, I'd love for the É accent to be literally the terminal of the hero V—not just visually similar. If someone overlaid the terminal from the hero V onto the accent, I would want them to match exactly. If possible, could you show a simple construction diagram of that relationship? I think confirming that one rule will give us complete confidence that the entire system is built from one signature gesture.

Second, I'd love the lowercase v to preserve just a touch more of the hero V's signature reach on the right arm. I don't expect it to be as obvious as the capital V—in fact, it should probably be almost imperceptible at first glance. But I think carrying that subtle extension into the lowercase will make the system feel even more proprietary and intentional. It's one of those details people may never consciously notice, but they'll feel that it belongs uniquely to Vellvé.

I think we're now refining the details that make a custom identity feel truly custom.

value_updates.accent_overlay_evaluation_rule: The É accent must be an exact one-to-one vector match with the approved Hero V terminal when overlaid.

decisions.reason: The exact overlay requirement applies to the É accent and Hero V terminal. The separate lowercase-v reach refinement from the same message is already represented in this candidate's history.
The approved Hero V terminal serves as the unchanged reference geometry; the source decision changes how the É accent must derive from it.
The source decision concerns the É accent rather than the supporting E and L letterform construction.
Exact derivation of the É accent does not change the second V's relative size or visual subordination to the Hero V.
The accent-to-terminal geometry rule does not change the deferred full-wordmark kerning requirement.
The source decision changes vector derivation geometry and does not alter the deferred champagne material treatment.
The requested exact accent derivation does not change the obligation to provide design rationale with review rounds.
